Not yet. Q and R both scored 1.00 on all 60 invoices, so this set no longer tells the configs apart. A perfect score that beats both predictions by 7 to 10 points can also come from a leaked answer key or a broken grader, so I will check for both once before we trust it.

What I do next:

1. Leak check. I scan the r05 trial transcripts for any read of the AP lead's reference fields, the graders, or spe/predictions/. I void any trial that looked at them.
2. Grader check. I rerun the grader selftest against the r05 grader. The oracle must pass, and an empty answer and a wrong answer must both fail. I also inspect the judge scores. A mean of exactly 7.0 for both configs on all 60 invoices can mean the judge returned a fixed default score. I assume 7 is not the top of the judge scale. If it is the top, the judge is at a ceiling too.
3. Close-out. In spe/prediction-log.md, I mark the r05 field accuracy predictions (0.93 for Q, 0.90 for R) as not scorable at a ceiling. The stop streak stays where it was. If either check finds a problem, I add it to spe/failures.md under the next F number. I put the original and regraded numbers side by side, then stop and report to you. If both checks come back clean, I add a "Proposed for round 6" table to spe/spec/spec.md and write spe/predictions/r06-draft.yaml with `status: draft`. I also update spe/README.md. Then I commit "SPE r05 learn: field accuracy at ceiling" and tag spe-r05. I do not push.

For round 6, I propose harder tasks or stricter graders. Harder tasks could be poor scans, multi-page line items, credit notes, and the PO mismatches the AP lead has seen cause trouble. A stricter grader could score each line item and the mismatch flag, not only the header fields. You decide whether we run round 6 or stop here. The loop counts as finished only after predictions hit for 3 rounds in a row, and this round does not count toward that.
